Jane — really helpful, thanks. Quick read-through below and a proposed sequencing that balances your procurement needs with our legal review cadence.

Summary proposal (high level):
1) Security questionnaire + evidence (SOC2 report, retention policy) submitted in parallel with initial MSA review. Security intake must be complete for DPA negotiation to proceed. Owner: Marcus Lin (security) / Redwood Legals for evidence handoff.
2) MSA redline window: 5 business days internal turn + 3 business days external review. If material privacy clauses are added, DPA redlines run in parallel with a mirrored 3-day external review. Owner: Laura Bennett (legal).
3) Order form (pricing & PO schedule): Drafted and agreed upon once MSA commercial terms are stable — can be provisionally agreed (signature contingent on final DPA) so Nexa can start PO approval. Owner: Karthik Iyer (account lead) + procurement contact.
4) Acceptance gates: Pilot handoff (technical sign-off by Nexa eng), Security acceptance (evidence validated), Commercial acceptance (PO received / order form signed). Only after security + commercial acceptance do we enable production keys.

Proposed timetable (target close in 3 weeks):
- Week 1: Security evidence exchange + MSA initial redlines (Nov 5–11)
- Week 2: DPA redlines & order-form pricing confirmation (Nov 12–18)
- Week 3: Exec signatures, PO issuance, and production enablement (Nov 19–25)

I copied Laura and Priyom for legal gating and for any redline constraints (e.g., data residency / audit windows). Marcus, can you confirm the exact SOC2 report we will share and the turnaround for cert verification?

Attachment: proposed_MAP_sequence.xlsx (internal)

Thanks — I can present this to Nexa procurement tomorrow if the legal owners confirm the gates.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP + timing clarity (MSA/DPA/order form)

Thanks for the outline, Karthik. A couple of legal notes and a tightened gating matrix so procurement can be precise about what to review at each step.

Legal gating matrix (concise):
- Security evidence (must be received before DPA moves to signature): SOC2 Type II report (latest) + data flow diagram + retention policy. Acceptable: current SOC2 + signed evidence transfer form. Owner: Marcus.
- MSA: we will accept commercial redlines on standard payment terms (NET 45 / thirty) with limited changes to IP and indemnity. Any customer-proposed indemnity caps or material changes trigger an exec review and may extend the MSA window. Owner: Laura.
- DPA: standard Redwood DPA applies; customer redlines focused on data subject rights will be reviewed but any non-standard deletion/portability obligations need legal sign-off and may require a contract rider. Owner: Priyom.
- Order form: We can accept a preliminary PO to start procurement approval, but provisioning requires final signatures on either (a) MSA + DPA or (b) an MSA with a signed order form and a conditional DPA commitment (with explicit date for DPA completion).

Risk callouts: if Nexa requires changes to data residency or encryption controls, that will push the DPA timeline by at least one additional week (controls evaluation + security acceptance).

I will review any redlines within 3 business days. Priyom — if you could pre-clear standard DPA concessions (list attached), it will speed this up.

Attachment: standard_dpa_concessions.pdf (summary)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
